title: Know what you hold
sub: From Only what you may see, in Data protection and privacy: why data has to be named before it can be protected, as Chile's front-of-pack warnings showed in 2016; five classes for a column, the strictest that applies, and four levels for a table, set once at the source by the data's owner; and the class following the column into everything made from it.
howto: The film is drawn in the module's look, Night glass: a dark hall of frosted panes, frosted where what's behind may not be read and clear where it may, with cards of near-clear frost and bright rims. Violet is personal data: each column's class is a chip, violet for a class of personal data and grey for none; a table's level is how frosted its pane is. Chile in 2012 and 2016 is painted in the same night light, with its place and year on a tag.
